references.text: Caleb, son of Jephunneh, is mentioned as one of the spies sent out from Kadesh-Barnea to explore Canaan.
Caleb encouraged the people and showed his faith that they could take the land, unlike the other spies.
The Lord promised that Caleb would be allowed to enter the land because he had a different spirit and followed the Lord wholeheartedly.
Caleb and Joshua were the only ones of the spies who would be allowed to enter the Promised Land.
Caleb the Kenizzite is mentioned as one who followed the Lord fully, along with Joshua.
Moses repeated the promise that Caleb would receive the land he had explored because he followed the Lord wholeheartedly.
Moses is referred to as God's man, the same title used in Joshua 14:6.
Gilgal was Israel's base during the conquest of Canaan, and it was there that Caleb came to Joshua.
Joshua blessed Caleb and gave him Hebron as an inheritance because he followed the Lord, the God of Israel, wholeheartedly.
Caleb, son of Jephunneh, received his portion among the sons of Judah, namely Hebron.
